memory_candidates: Lean4 pattern: when weakening a bridge lemma's hypothesis from a full N-conjunct predicate `P` to a single named conjunct `Q` (strictly weaker), prefer introducing `Q` as a standalone named `def` plus a one-line `.k` projection theorem from `P` to `Q`, rather than editing `P`'s own body in place. This avoids any risk to `P`'s existing `rfl`-based bridge lemmas (e.g. an `_eq` bridge to a generic-driver form) and lets both `P` and any structurally-parallel sibling predicate (e.g. a bifurcated variant) share `Q` verbatim.

Lean4 gotcha: when a `ReflTransGen`-path bridge lemma unwraps a modal formula at the path's endpoint (e.g. strips `□`/`◇` via a `_self`-style base case), a caller that needs the *wrapped* formula preserved at some intermediate point on the path (not the endpoint) needs a separate 'preserving' bridge -- the exact same induction skeleton, but with the `refl` case returning the hypothesis unchanged instead of invoking the unwrapping step. The two bridges are not interchangeable even though both consume the same underlying single-step lemma.
